patterns: An error occurred while attempting to reference the specified entry
entries.cause: bcdedit was aimed at {current}. That identifier does not exist in an offline BCD store or in WinRE, and braces are mangled when the command is sent through a shell.
entries.detection: bcdedit prints that it cannot reference the specified entry.
entries.rollback: Export a fresh BCD before the next set. Do not import a store that was edited with {current}.
repair_order: Run bcdedit as an argument list, with no shell.
Choose the Windows Boot Loader whose device or osdevice is partition=<system drive>.
Use that GUID. If none matches, use {default}.
After /set, run /enum and require device and osdevice to be partition=C:.

entries.name: ERROR_INVALID_NAME
entries.cause: bcdboot received a /s target that is not a bare drive letter, a missing or quoted Windows directory, or /f ALL while the firmware mode is unknown.
entries.detection: bcdboot exits 123. The log says the filename, directory name, or volume label syntax is incorrect.
repair_order: Confirm %SystemRoot% exists and pass it as its own list item, with no extra quotes.
Read the live drive map and take the ESP or system volume letter.
If the volume is only a folder mount or a \\?\Volume{GUID}\ path, assign a temporary letter with mountvol, then Add-PartitionAccessPath, then diskpart assign letter=.
Pass /s as S: with no trailing slash and no quotes.
Do not pass /f ALL when the firmware mode is unknown.
Treat exit 123 as failure. Re-read bcdedit /enum {bootmgr} and the ESP files before any GO.
entries.rollback: Remove only the temporary letter this attempt assigned. Leave the previous boot files in place.

entries.name: ERROR_DISK_FULL
entries.cause: The ESP does not have enough free space for bcdboot. A 96 MB ASUS ESP is full when boot fonts and extra locale folders are present.
entries.detection: bcdboot exits 112, or the ESP free space measured before the call is below 32 MB.
repair_order: Measure free space on the mounted ESP before bcdboot.
Back up EFI\Microsoft\Boot\Fonts, then remove the font files.
Back up unused locale folders and remove them. Keep en-US and the current UI locale.
Remove leftover temp and backup files this tool created under EFI\MagicUpgrade.
Retry bcdboot with /l and that one locale.
Do not shrink or create a partition unless MAGIC_ESP_EXPAND=1. This repair never resizes.
Treat exit 112 as failure. Re-read bcdedit /enum {bootmgr} and the ESP files before any GO.
entries.rollback: Restore the backed-up fonts and locale folders from esp-space-backups. Do not delete the BCD or bootmgfw.efi.

patterns: arguments specified for this command are not valid
entries.detection: diskpart stdout, English or French, after a script command.

syntax.windows-8-and-later: select volume <n> then assign letter=S or remove letter=S. select disk <n> and select partition <n> before active or set id. No trailing colon on the letter.

entries.rollback: Do not continue the script. Export the BCD store before any later import.

entries.detection: diskpart or Service Control text naming the Virtual Disk service.

syntax.windows-8-and-later: diskpart rescan, after the Virtual Disk service is running. rescan only locates disks; it does not repair a bad command.

entries.rollback: Stop if rescan does not change the disk list. Do not clean or convert.

entries.detection: First 512 bytes of the system volume do not end in 55 AA, or the BIOS boot text names an invalid partition table.
entries.rollback: The previous volume boot sector is not restored by bootsect. Restore the pre-op partition backup if the signature check still fails.

entries.detection: MBR boot partition is present but not marked active.

syntax.windows-8-and-later: select disk <n> then select partition <n> then active. active applies only to MBR.

entries.rollback: Do not mark a second partition active. Restore the pre-op backup if boot still fails.

entries.detection: EFI\Microsoft\Boot\bootmgfw.efi is missing on the ESP.
entries.rollback: bcdboot /c does not keep the previous BCD elements. Import the exported store if the new store does not verify.

entries.detection: BIOS boot manager file is missing from the system partition.
entries.rollback: Keep the exported BCD and the pre-op copy of bootmgr. bootrec /fixmbr replaces only the MBR code, not the partition table.

entries.detection: The BCD file is missing or its hash does not match the expected pre-op record.

syntax.windows-vista-and-later: bcdedit /export <file> then bcdedit /import <file>. bcdedit /createstore creates an empty store that is not the system store.

entries.rollback: Import is valid only for a file previously created by /export. Import deletes the current system-store entries first.

entries.detection: bcdedit /enum all fails to open the store, or device and osdevice do not name an existing partition.

syntax.windows-vista-and-later: bcdedit /set {default} device partition=C: and bcdedit /set {default} osdevice partition=C: and bcdedit /set {bootmgr} device partition=S:

entries.rollback: Export the current store before /set or /import. Re-import the export if the following /enum is not a known-good store.

entries.detection: bcdedit /enum firmware does not list Windows Boot Manager.

syntax.windows-8-and-later: bcdboot C:\Windows /s S: /f UEFI /l en-us. /s does not itself create the NVRAM entry; omit /s when the ESP is the firmware system partition and an NVRAM entry is required.

entries.rollback: If /s was required to target a specific ESP, confirm the firmware list after reboot before deleting the previous boot entry.

entries.detection: The GPT system partition is not type c12a7328-f81f-11d2-ba4b-00a0c93ec93b and is not marked system.

syntax.windows-8-and-later: bcdboot C:\Windows /s S: /f UEFI. set id on a GPT disk uses the GUID form with override and only after select partition.

entries.rollback: Do not change the partition type unless the pre-op backup of the partition table exists.

entries.detection: The live disk scan did not return a map.
entries.rollback: A failed rescan is not a reason to clean a disk.

entries.detection: Boot status 0xc000000e: the boot selection failed because a required device is inaccessible.

syntax.windows-vista-and-later: bcdedit /set {default} device partition=C: and bcdedit /set {default} osdevice partition=C: and bcdedit /set {bootmgr} device partition=C:

entries.rollback: Export the BCD store before /set. The Microsoft recovery note for this status is to correct unknown device values, not to recreate partitions.

entries.detection: WinRE or Setup text contains status 0xc0000225.
entries.rollback: Repair the boot files from the installed Windows directory. Do not format the Windows volume.

entries.detection: WinRE or Setup text contains status 0xc000000f.

syntax.windows-8-and-later: bcdboot C:\Windows /s S: /f UEFI or bcdboot C:\Windows /s S: /f BIOS

entries.rollback: Import the exported BCD if the rebuilt store does not enumerate a known-good loader.

entries.detection: WinRE or Setup text contains status 0xc0000098.
entries.rollback: Replace only the missing boot file from the Windows Boot directory or from bcdboot. Keep the pre-op ESP copy.

entries.detection: Stop 0x7B during startup, including after an upgrade rollback.

syntax.windows-10-and-later: In WinRE: DISM /image:C:\ /get-packages and, for a pending package, DISM /Image:C:\ /Cleanup-Image /RevertPendingActions

entries.rollback: Filter edits and package removal are destructive. Confirm the Windows directory letter in WinRE before /image.

entries.detection: Setup result 0xC1900101 with extend code 0x20017.

syntax.windows-10-and-later: No single repair command. Update storage and network drivers, remove conflicting security software, then retry Setup.

entries.rollback: 0xC1900101 means Setup rolled back. Read $Windows.~BT\Sources\Rollback before changing boot files.

entries.detection: Setup result 0xC1900101 without a more specific extend code. This is a generic rollback, usually a driver.

syntax.windows-10-and-later: Review setupmem.dmp and setupapi.dev.log under $Windows.~BT\Sources\Rollback, then retry from a clean boot.

entries.rollback: Setup already restored the previous OS. Do not run boot repairs unless the extend code is a boot phase.

entries.detection: Setup.exe reports the computer does not meet minimum requirements.

syntax.windows-10-and-later: No bypass on the first attempt. Confirm the published requirement list, then retry.

entries.rollback: Do not change partitions because of this code alone.

entries.detection: Setup compatibility block in the same family as other 0xC19002xx requirement failures.

syntax.windows-10-and-later: Read the compatibility report in the Setup logs before any second attempt.

entries.rollback: The first attempt stays an official upgrade without boot changes.

entries.detection: A previous setup cleanup is still pending and the computer must restart.

syntax.windows-10-and-later: Restart, then run Setup again. If it persists, clean temporary and system files with Disk Cleanup.

entries.rollback: Do not delete $Windows.~BT until after the required restart.

entries.detection: Setup extend codes 0x80070070-0x50011, 0x50012, or 0x60000: not enough free space.

syntax.windows-10-and-later: Free disk space and retry. The published Windows 10 figures are 16 GB for 32-bit and 20 GB for 64-bit.

entries.rollback: Do not shrink the Windows volume below the space Setup still needs.

entries.detection: 0x80070002 with extend 0x20009 during partition analysis, often a second system disk.

syntax.windows-10-and-later: Disconnect the unused system disk and retry. Delete that system partition only when it is known to be unused.

entries.rollback: Reconnect the data disk after Setup. Do not delete a partition that still holds a bootable Windows.

entries.detection: Secure Boot certificate status or event 1801. Event 1808 indicates the 2023 certificates and boot manager update completed.

syntax.windows-11: Update OEM firmware first. Windows then applies the Secure Boot certificate update. Do not replace bootmgfw.efi with an unsigned copy.

entries.rollback: Do not delete the 2011 CA until the device boots with the 2023-signed Windows Boot Manager.

entries.detection: dbx or SBAT revocation text, including event 1796 while a certificate update is applied.

syntax.windows-11: Check db before dbx. A dbx match must block the image. Update KEK so later db and dbx updates can apply.

entries.rollback: Do not clear dbx to force a revoked loader to boot.

entries.detection: reagentc /info shows Windows RE disabled or the image path missing.
entries.rollback: /disable removes the current RE registration. Record reagentc /info output first.

entries.detection: The computer does not start after updates and WinRE shows a pending package.
entries.rollback: Confirm the offline Windows letter before /image. RevertPendingActions undoes pending updates.

entries.detection: BIOS startup repair needs boot code rewritten. Fixmbr does not repair a damaged partition table.

syntax.windows-7-and-later: bootrec /fixmbr then bootrec /fixboot. For BCD: bcdedit /export then bootrec /rebuildbcd

entries.rollback: Export BCD before rebuildbcd. Do not use fixmbr as the UEFI repair; use bcdboot /f UEFI.

entries.detection: Firmware or a log says GRUB rescue. The Linux loader is what failed, not a reason to delete other EFI directories.

syntax.notes: Boot-Repair reinstalls GRUB and writes a Boot-Info report. This project keeps the Linux EFI tree and still uses bcdboot only for the Windows loader.

entries.rollback: Restore the ESP file backup before any GRUB reinstall. Do not format the EFI partition.

tools.name: Startup Repair
tools.license: Microsoft Windows, no separate open-source grant
tools.does: Windows automatic repair from WinRE. It is the signed path this project prefers.

tools.name: bootrec
tools.license: Microsoft Windows, no separate open-source grant
tools.does: fixmbr rewrites master boot code only. fixboot rewrites the boot sector. scanos and rebuildbcd rebuild the store after an export.

tools.name: bcdboot
tools.license: Microsoft Windows, no separate open-source grant
tools.does: Copies boot files from a Windows directory. /f UEFI, BIOS, or ALL. /f requires /s.

tools.name: bcdedit
tools.license: Microsoft Windows, no separate open-source grant
tools.does: Exports, imports, and creates BCD stores, and sets device and osdevice.

tools.name: bootsect
tools.license: Microsoft Windows, no separate open-source grant
tools.does: Writes Bootmgr-compatible boot code with /nt60 and can update the MBR with /mbr.

tools.name: SetupDiag
tools.does: Reads Setup logs and writes SetupDiagResults.xml. It does not change the disk.

tools.name: DISM
tools.license: Microsoft Windows, no separate open-source grant
tools.does: Offline image repair. /get-packages then /Cleanup-Image /RevertPendingActions for a pending update that blocks boot.

tools.name: SFC
tools.license: Microsoft Windows, no separate open-source grant
tools.does: Offline system-file check from WinRE with /offbootdir and /offwindir after the Windows letter is confirmed.

tools.name: reagentc
tools.license: Microsoft Windows, no separate open-source grant
tools.does: Enables the signed Winre.wim recovery image.

tools.name: Media Creation Tool
tools.license: Microsoft, free download, not open source
tools.does: Builds official Windows installation media. This project does not redistribute it.

tools.name: Boot-Repair
tools.does: One-click boot repair with a backup and a Boot-Info report, including GRUB reinstall. Idea used here: back up first and keep a written diagnosis. No Boot-Repair code is included.

tools.name: rEFInd
tools.does: EFI boot manager that scans for loaders. Idea used here: identify bootmgfw.efi before rewriting it. No rEFInd code is included. The original rEFIt tree is BSD; the rEFInd changes are GPL-3.0.

tools.name: OpenCore
tools.does: UEFI boot loader. This project already has an optional OpenDuet chain and does not vendor OpenCore source in this change.

tools.name: GRUB
tools.does: Chainloads Windows from an EFI or BIOS menu. Idea used here: do not delete the Linux EFI directory while repairing Windows.

tools.name: SystemRescue
tools.does: Live Linux rescue disk. The optional Linux plan does not download or write it.

tools.name: TestDisk
tools.does: Recovers partition tables. It is a manual last resort and is not launched by this project.

tools.name: ms-sys
tools.does: Writes a Microsoft-compatible boot record from Linux. This project uses Windows bootsect instead and does not ship ms-sys or its embedded boot records. ms-sys-free is the fork without those records.

tools.name: EasyBCD
tools.does: Edits the Windows boot menu. Idea used here: a visible menu entry and a one-time boot sequence. No EasyBCD code or installer is included.

tools.name: Rufus
tools.does: Writes a bootable USB stick. Idea used here: do not treat media as bootable until the partition type and boot files verify. No Rufus code is included.
